items.statement: Loan of INR258 crores to associate Zuari Agro Chemicals expected to be repaid in current quarter
items.quote: We also expect that the loan that was given to an associate company, Zuari Agro Chemicals Limited, will also be repaid to the company in the current quarter.

items.statement: ICD income from group companies increased unallocated income to INR13.7 crores year-on-year
items.quote: The income which has increased on account of unallocated is the ICD's income that we have given to our group companies.

items.statement: Plan to consolidate investments by buying shares of Zuari International for INR150 crores in tranches
items.quote: We have taken an ICD approval and the strategy behind this transaction is that we want to consolidate the investments which are there in our different companies at the holding group level.

items.statement: Received AED55 million (INR142.58 crores) from Dubai St. Regis project profit repatriation in current quarter
items.quote: So we have in the current quarter received AED55 million, which in Indian rupee terms translates to INR142.58 crores.

items.statement: Guidance for INR900 crores profit repatriation from Dubai project in current financial year, balance INR758 crores on track
items.quote: And we had projected that we will receive up to INR900 crores in the current financial year. And I should say that we are on track to receive the balance amount.

items.statement: Other expenses normalized at INR14-15 crores per quarter during sugar mill repair and maintenance period
items.quote: Our other expenses remain in the range of INR14 crores to INR15 crores every quarter because this is a period during which we do repair and maintenance for our sugar division.

items.statement: Promoters infused INR20 crores capital, INR15 crores already deployed for new brands
items.quote: the promoters have already infused money when we needed the capital for new brands and it was primarily for new brands. And we infused INR20 crores of promoter capital. Out of the INR20 crores, I think INR15 crores is already into the system.

items.statement: Revenue increased 20% in Q1 FY27 driven by Jharsuguda plant contribution from existing products
items.quote: We have a good 20% increase in our revenue this year, thanks to Jharsuguda from our existing products.

items.statement: Free cash flow averaged INR8-9 crores over last 3-4 years; target is INR13-14 crores by growing systems revenue to INR30 crores
items.quote: On an average we do around INR8 to INR9 crores of free cash flow in the last 3-4 years. This year I think we should be able to do -- see we are in the pipeline, there are 2-3 interesting things that have happened.

items.statement: Wages paid first, then bill raised on client with typical 3-month DSO cycle; minimum wage increases passed on contractually but with time lag
items.quote: Yes, so we of course give the wages first and then we raise a bill on the client and then the client pays typically in three months. That is our DSO cycle.

items.statement: Short-term loans and advances include amounts to related parties such as Keertika Academy
items.quote: And these also include loans and advances to related parties such as Keertika Academy.

items.statement: Consolidated inventory was INR96.8 crores as of June 30, 2026, with INR84.4 crores at overseas subsidiaries, deliberately positioned for faster customer response.
items.quote: As of June 30, 2026, our consolidated inventory stood at about INR96.8 crores, with around INR84.4 crores positioned at our overseas subsidiaries.

items.statement: Inventory conversion cycle runs over 2 quarters; management expects similar inventory levels going forward, adjusting to demand and supply.
items.quote: Well, the business cycle inherently runs over 2 quarters at least in our business. So, as on the closing date of the reporting period, I think that may have been the figure. But I think over the next 2 quarters of that closing date or 1.5 quarters, I think it will get converted and then new inventory will again come into play.

items.statement: Working capital cycles expected to remain elongated due to geopolitical situation; inventory levels to stay in lower double digits.
items.quote: So, I think working capital cycles will be similar to what we are absorbing right now for the time being. And we hope to improve it as soon as the market or the global markets and situations cool down. And about the inventories as well, I think similar levels, plus or minus a few percentage points, in double digits, I believe, lower double digits, we can expect going forward as well.

items.statement: Increase in debtors is a planned strategy for overseas market penetration; longer shipping times also extend debtor cycles.
items.quote: Well, I mean, the increase of debtors is a planned strategy of penetration in overseas markets. And as we are deploying manpower and people in those areas, so it is for the purpose to sell locally in those regions, achieve higher growth in sales. And I bel ieve that is the part of the reason of increase in debtors

items.statement: Equity component of INR350 crore for cell line structured as NCDs and CCDs progressing through due diligence
items.quote: the equity component of INR350 crore structured as a combination of NCDs and CCDs is progressing through the due diligence stage.

items.statement: Working capital cycle targeted at 60-70 days by FY28 from current 100-120 days
items.quote: By FY28, we expect an operating cycle with the much more controlled and disciplined working capital structure, with a targeting days of 60 to 70 days.

items.statement: Operating cash flow generation is decent; free cash flow to improve as working capital efficiency increases
items.quote: This is particularly important because Simplex is already generating a very decent cash flow from operations. As working capital becomes efficient, a greater portion of our operating cash generation should translate into free cash flows rather than remaining tied up in the operation cycles.

items.statement: Railway bogies have 30-45 day cycle; RXIL/Invoice Mart platforms give payments in 30-35 days post-dispatch
items.quote: Secondly, is the RXIL and this Invoice Mart platforms from whom we have already got registered and are getting payments. Roughly around 30 to 35 days in a timeline after dispatch.

items.statement: Bill discounting on RXIL/Invoice Mart at 5-5.5% interest rate for early payment
items.quote: They discount the bills at somewhere around 5 to 5.5% rate of interest. We get an early payments on that.

items.statement: At 300 crore revenue and 60-day cycle, working capital requirement estimated around 50 crores
items.quote: So 60 days will end up at so 300 crores we'll only need probably around what 50 crores of working capital. That's a fair understanding, right? Avinash Hariharno: Yes, yes

items.statement: Debtors reduced to 65 days revenue in June 2026 from 70 days in March 2026
items.quote: The working capital management continued to remain excellent, with debtors reducing to 65 days' revenue in June 26, down from 70 days' revenue in March 2026.

items.statement: Cash balance healthy at Rs 2.1 billion as on 30 June 2026, free cash flow Rs 644 million
items.quote: Cash balance continues to be healthy at Rs 2.1 billion as on 30 June 26, of which free cash flow is Rs 644 million.

items.statement: Other income is interest earned on IPO funds parked in DC projects
items.quote: That is interest income from the DC projects. Vipul Makwana: Okay. Management: This is related to the IPO funds that we have received and parked in DC projects, so the other income is essentially the interest earned on those funds

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 11.5 crore allocated to Mathura project from total IPO size of Rs 29.42 crore
items.quote: The Mathura project has a total project cost of ₹49 crore. Out of this, around ₹17 crore will be funded internally, of which ₹11.5 crore is the IPO component, and the balance will be managed through other sources.

items.statement: Inventory increased to INR228.35 crores due to new higher-margin products and monsoon impact on sales; expected to normalize below INR200 crores after Diwali
items.quote: First, we have added some additional products that yield higher margins. Second, during the June quarter, there is a minor monsoon impact, due to which sales remain slightly lower while production continues. Therefore, inventory remains slightly higher in the June and September quarters.

items.statement: Inventory expected to normalize below INR200 crores after Diwali
items.quote: This will normalize after Diwali. After Diwali, it will come below INR200 crores.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 148 days from 168 days previous quarter
items.quote: Cash conversion cycle has improved to 148 days from 168 days in the previous quarter, with Vriddhi Council cost savings of ₹19.1 crore realised to date against a ₹50 crore annual target.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 148 days compared to 170 last quarter
items.quote: So our cash conversion cycle has actually reduced to 148 days compared to 170 last quarter.

items.statement: Focus on reducing inventory, improving collections, payment terms and bill discounting for faster cash flows
items.quote: A big part of our effort has been on reducing inventory which is non-moving, or indirect materials inventory, and focusing on direct materials which are required for sales.

items.statement: Plans to raise equity in future with promoters participating alongside other participants
items.quote: We do have plans to raise equity in the future. There are multiple options that we are evaluating, and the promoters themselves would be putting in equity along with other participants.

items.statement: Capex of ₹30 crore for FY27 to be funded 75% debt and 25% internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, the capex is going to be funded by a combination of debt and internal accruals. So we're looking at 75% funding from debt and 25% from internal accruals.

items.statement: Promoter shares pledged to Neo Asset Management as security for loan; expected to be released after refinancing within 1-1.5 years; promoter holding increased to 48-49%
items.quote: As part of the transaction with Neo Asset Management, the promoters' shares are being pledged as security against the loan. This is intended to be a short-term, higher-cost arrangement, and we expect to refinance through banks within approximately one to one-and-a-half years, following stabilisation of the machine and improvement in the Company's financial performance. At that stage, the shares ar

items.statement: CFO position changed; leadership changes in Wrap & Carry business and CFO role for different reasons; objective to strengthen leadership stability
items.quote: Changes have been made in the leadership of the Wrap & Carry business and in the CFO position for different reasons. While it is not possible to guarantee that no further changes will occur, our objective is to strengthen le adership stability and organisational continuity

items.statement: Interest outflow under Neo transaction estimated at ₹120-122 crore vs ₹150-155 crore under previous bank structure; net cash outflow lower despite higher stated rate
items.quote: Under the earlier bank structure, total interest outflow between 1 April 2026 and 31 March 2028 was estimated at approximately ₹150 crore –₹155 crore. Under the present transaction, despite the higher stated interest rate, the estimated aggregate outflow is approximately ₹120 crore –₹122 crore. While the arrangement has an impact on the profit and loss account, it improves the projected cash-flow

items.statement: Neo Asset Management invested ₹30 crore in equity as part of structured transaction to fund Project Jagriti
items.quote: Neo has also demonstrated confidence in the Company by investing ₹30 crore in equity.

items.statement: Management confirmed a warrant allotment of 2 lakh warrants to Rikhav Securities Limited as a non-promoter investor.
items.quote: I think yes this is just as an investor, he has come. So it is a small amount. It is a very, very -- a small company is always a challenge to get the investor.

items.statement: Collections typically take 60 to 90 days, up to 120 days in some states
items.quote: So collections are typically the same right now. You can say minimum 60 to 90 days. Very -- I think a few states, say, in the Northeast or where accessibility becomes an issue, it might go up to 120 days, but not more than that.

items.statement: Acquired 40% stake in Quebec Petroleum as an associate; profits will be added to consolidated financials.
items.quote: since we are going with that investment as an associate and not as a subsidiary. So initially we have acquired a 40% stake. So their profits are also going to get added in our consolidated balance sheets and financials.

items.statement: Promoter has significant holding and is directly involved in daily operations and growth decisions.
items.quote: The first is the promoter's skin in the game. The promoter has a significant holding in the company and is working day and night for the company's growth.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to final and pre-final bills pending for three completed projects; inventory rose from advance material procurement in February-March due to price increases.
items.quote: So trade receivable has increased because the final bill and pre-final bill was there for these projects, and it always takes time to realize payments of the final and prefinal bills.

items.statement: Receivable days are high because final bills are pending for NBCC Aligarh and Telecommunications India projects; expects to close Aligarh billing by 15th September and telecom projects by 30th September.
items.quote: Receivable days are a little high nowadays because final bills are still pending in our three projects like NBCC Aligarh project and Telecomnunications India Limited, two projects we have completed, but the funds are - final bill and final approval, all things are pending

items.statement: Company has not availed mobilization advance for new projects including IIT and Bathinda despite 10% clause being available, preferring to use internal funds.
items.quote: We have just received a project IIT [inaudible 0:23:37]. We can take mobilization advance, but we have not availed the mobilization advance till now. It is an interest-bearing advance.

items.statement: Operating cash profit was about 12-12.5 crores in Q1 FY27; working capital increased due to high copper prices and capex of 4.2 crores was incurred.
items.quote: The operating cash profit was fairly healthy for the Q1, I'd say about 12-12 and a half crores, but of course, working capital has also gone up.

items.statement: Raised INR52.93 crores through rights issue for working capital and general corporate purposes
items.quote: During Q1, we raised INR52.93 crores through the rights issue. This provides additional resource for working capital and general corporate purpose, and give us greater flexibility to support our expansion plan and customers' requirement.
